name: ScanProsite_scan_protein
description: Scan a protein against the PROSITE database of protein motifs, domains, and families. Given a UniProt accession (e.g., P04637 for TP53, P01308 for insulin), identifies all PROSITE pattern matches in the protein sequence. Returns matched PROSITE signature accessions and IDs with start/end positions. PROSITE is part of the ExPASy/SIB suite and contains 1,800+ patterns and profiles for protein functional sites and domains. Essential for identifying conserved motifs like zinc fingers, kinase activation loops, or receptor binding sites. Note: only patterns (PS00xxx) are scanned; profile matches require the ScanProsite web interface.

seq.description: UniProt accession to scan for PROSITE motifs. Examples: 'P04637' (TP53, returns PS00348 p53 signature), 'P01308' (insulin, returns PS00262 insulin family), 'Q9UHC1' (MLH3, returns PS00058 DNA mismatch repair). Can also accept a raw amino acid sequence.

n_match.description: Number of PROSITE motif matches found

n_seq.description: Number of sequences scanned (1 for single protein)

sequence_ac.description: UniProt accession of the scanned protein

sequence_db.description: Sequence database (sp for Swiss-Prot, tr for TrEMBL)

start.description: Start position of the motif match in the protein

stop.description: End position of the motif match

signature_ac.description: PROSITE accession (e.g., PS00348 for p53 family signature)

signature_id.description: PROSITE entry name (e.g., P53, INSULIN, DNA_MISMATCH_REPAIR_1)

level_tag.description: Match confidence level tag (0 = strong match)

matchset.description: Array of PROSITE motif matches with positions

name: ScanProsite_find_proteins_with_motif
description: Reverse PROSITE motif scan with recoverable pagination over every match present in the ScanProsite response. Continue with next_offset while has_more is true. If capped is true, the remote database scan itself is incomplete even after all available pages are consumed; complete_database_result and capped_note make this explicit.

signature_ac.description: PROSITE signature accession starting with 'PS'. Examples: 'PS00029' (LEUCINE_ZIPPER), 'PS00107' (PROTEIN_KINASE_ATP), 'PS00028' (ZINC_FINGER_C2H2_1). Use PROSITE_search or PROSITE_get_entry to discover signature accessions.

db.description: Sequence database to search: 'sprot' = Swiss-Prot (reviewed, default), 'trembl' = TrEMBL (unreviewed), 'uniprot' = both.

skip_frequent.description: If true (default), skip very frequent low-information signatures (SKIP-FLAG=TRUE patterns such as PS00005, PS00008). Set to false to force ScanProsite to include them; note these can produce extremely large or truncated responses across the whole proteome.

max_results.description: Maximum response matches to return on this page (default 50, max 1000).

offset.description: Zero-based offset within matches available in this ScanProsite response.

sequence_ac.description: UniProt accession of the matching protein (e.g., Q6GZW6)

sequence_db.description: Sequence database (sp for Swiss-Prot, tr for TrEMBL)

start.description: Start position of the motif match in the protein

stop.description: End position of the motif match

signature_ac.description: PROSITE signature accession that matched (e.g., PS00029)

oneOf.description: Array of matching UniProt proteins with motif positions
